description: This topic deals with solving mathematical expressions and finding their nearest values. It is highly important for increasing calculation speed in competitive exams.

sections.title: VBODMAS Rule
sections.description: The correct sequence for solving any complex mathematical expression is determined by the VBODMAS rule.

key_concepts.explanation: A line drawn over numbers. It is solved first in an expression.
Solve brackets after the bar. Order: Round ( ), then Curly { }, and finally Square [ ].
'Of' means multiplication, but it is solved before standard division and multiplication.
After that, perform division (÷), multiplication (x), addition (+), and finally subtraction (-).

sections.title: Rules of Approximation
sections.description: Approximation is used to convert decimal numbers into their nearest easy whole numbers.

cases.condition: When the digit after the decimal is >= 5
results: Example: 45.68 is considered 46 and 124.89 is considered 125.

cases.condition: When the digit after the decimal is < 5
results: Example: 45.32 is considered 45 and 124.19 is considered 124.

sections.title: Important Algebraic Formulas
sections.description: Standard algebraic identities are used directly to quickly solve simplification problems.

sections.title: Percentage and Fraction Conversion
sections.description: Memorizing fractional values of common percentages is essential for speeding up multiplication and division in simplification.

sections.title: Steps to Find Square Root and Cube Root
sections.description: Using approximation to find the roots of numbers that are not perfect squares or cubes.

steps.title: Find nearest perfect square or cube
steps.detail: Find the perfect square or cube closest to the given number (let's assume it is 'x').

steps.title: Find the difference
steps.detail: Calculate the difference between the given number and the perfect square 'x' (let's assume it is 'y'). Write the number as x ± y.

steps.title: Square Root Approximation Formula
steps.detail: Use the formula: √(x ± y) ≈ √x ± (y / 2√x). Substitute the values and solve to get the approximate answer.
